manual_title: NDMA National Disaster Management Guidelines: Management of Floods
section_ref: Section 4.2 & 7.1 — Early Warning, Embankment Breach & Floodplain Evacuation
authority: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Govt. of India
summary: Standard operating procedures when river gauges cross Warning Level (WL) or Danger Level (DL), or when 24-hour rainfall exceeds 150 mm in low-lying alluvial plains.
official_directives: Trigger Stage-1 (Yellow) alert when river water level reaches within 1.0m of Danger Level; pre-position NDRF/SDRF inflatable motorized boats (IRBs) at block headquarters.
Trigger Stage-2 (Orange) mandatory lateral evacuation of vulnerable groups (infants, pregnant women, senior citizens, disabled) to designated flood shelters above the 100-year HFL contour.
Inspect earthen river embankments (bunds) every 4 hours for piping, seepage, or toe erosion; deploy geo-textile sandbag ring-bunds immediately upon detecting boils.
Prohibit all vehicular movement across submersible causeways and bridges once water overflows the deck by 15 cm (6 inches).

manual_title: IMD RSMC New Delhi Cyclone Warning & 4-Stage Coastal Alert Protocol
section_ref: Section 2.1 & 5.4 — Pre-Cyclone Watch, Yellow Alert, Orange Warning & Red Post-Landfall Outlook
authority: India Meteorological Department (IMD RSMC New Delhi)
summary: Official 4-stage color-coded cyclone warning timeline and marine/coastal operational actions for North Indian Ocean tropical cyclones.
official_directives: Stage-1 Pre-Cyclone Watch (72 hours prior): Issue early bulletin to Chief Secretaries and Maritime Boards; advise deep-sea fishing vessels to return to harbor immediately.

Stage-2 Cyclone Alert / Yellow (48 hours prior): Broadcast hourly coastal bulletins; initiate preparation of Multipurpose Cyclone Shelters (MPCS) with 7-day dry rations, drinking water, and DG gensets.

Stage-3 Cyclone Warning / Orange (24 hours prior): Execute 100% evacuation of kutcha houses and low-lying coastal Gram Panchayats within 10 km of shoreline; suspend rail, port, and aviation operations along the landfall cone.

Stage-4 Post-Landfall Outlook / Red (12 hours prior to landfall & during passage): Enforce strict indoor shelter lock-in during eye passage (warn citizens not to step outdoors during the temporary calm inside the cyclone eye).

manual_title: INCOIS & NDMA Coastal Storm Surge & Estuarine Tidal Backwater Manual
section_ref: Section 3.3 — Storm Surge Inundation Envelopes & Outfall Sluice Gate Operations
authority: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) & NDMA
summary: Operational protocol for compound coastal flooding where cyclonic onshore winds coincide with astronomical high tide, impeding river and urban gravity drainage.
official_directives: Pre-drain coastal retention ponds and urban stormwater canals during the low-tide window 12–18 hours prior to projected cyclone landfall.
Close tidal regulator sluice gates and backflow flap valves 2 hours before astronomical high tide to prevent saline sea-surge ingress into freshwater canals and agricultural polders.
Evacuate all settlements below 5.0m Mean Sea Level (MSL) within the projected 34-knot onshore wind quadrant due to bathymetric surge amplification.
Seal domestic borewell casing heads with watertight neoprene caps prior to surge arrival to prevent aquifer salinization.

manual_title: NDRF Standard Operating Procedure: Urban Flood Search, Rescue & Boat Triage
section_ref: Section 1.1 & 3.2 — Priority Rescue Triage (P1–P4) & Rooftop/Air-Lift Operations
authority: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ministry of Home Affairs
summary: Life-safety triage matrix for prioritizing boat and helicopter extraction during acute flash floods and cyclone inundation.
official_directives: Priority-1 (CRITICAL_P1 — Immediate Dispatch <30 min): Citizens trapped on rooftops/vehicles/trees with water rising above chest/ground-floor ceiling, life-support medical patients (dialysis, oxygen, cardiac), infants, and pregnant women.
Priority-2 (HIGH_P2 — Urgent Dispatch <90 min): Ground-floor apartments with 0.5m–1.2m water ingress, stranded senior citizens, and structurally compromised kutcha dwellings.
Instruct rooftop-stranded citizens to NEVER enter enclosed attics without exterior hatches; signal USAR boats/aircraft using high-visibility orange fabric, mirrors, or 3 whistle blasts.
Maintain a minimum 3-meter clearance from submerged transformers, feeder pillars, and fallen overhead power lines during inflatable boat approach.

manual_title: CEA & NDMA Electrical Grid Isolation & Substation Flood Safety Protocol
section_ref: Section 6.1 — Preventive Feeder De-energization & Domestic MCB Shutdown
summary: Mandatory electrical isolation procedures to prevent fatal water electrification during urban waterlogging and cyclonic windfalls.
official_directives: Household Level: Switch OFF the Main Circuit Breaker (MCB) and ELCB/RCCB immediately before rising floodwater reaches 15 cm (below wall socket height). Never touch electrical switchgear while standing on wet floors.
DISCOM Feeder Level: De-energize 11kV/33kV distribution transformers and pillar boxes when surrounding water depth reaches 30 cm above plinth level or when wind speeds exceed 75 km/h.
Treat all downed overhead conductors and submerged street-light poles as LIVE; establish a 10-meter exclusion zone until DISCOM line staff verify grounding.
Do not re-energize flooded residential wiring until insulation resistance (Megger test) and earth continuity are certified by a licensed electrician.

manual_title: MoHUA Urban Flooding Standard Operating Procedure: Pluvial Drainage & Underpasses
section_ref: Section 5.2 — Underpass Barricading, Dewatering Pump Deployment & Traffic Diversion
authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Govt. of India
summary: Municipal command room protocol for extreme convective cloudbursts (>50 mm/hour) and urban stormwater surcharge.
official_directives: Automatically close and barricade all road underpasses and rail subways when water depth reaches 25 cm; activate red LED flood-depth gauges.

Vehicle Escape Rule: 30 cm (12 inches) of moving water floats passenger cars; 60 cm (24 inches) sweeps away SUVs and trucks. If stalled, unbuckle immediately, roll down or break side window, climb onto car roof, and dial 112.
Prohibit entry into underground basement parking lots during Red/Orange rainfall alerts; deploy mobile high-head diesel dewatering pumps at chronic depression sumps.
Clear solid waste and plastic choke points from storm-drain trash racks every 2 hours during active monsoon spells.

manual_title: NDMA Guidelines: Medical Preparedness, Chronic Care & Post-Flood Epidemic Control
section_ref: Section 8.4 — Dialysis/Oxygen Continuity, Snakebite Anti-Venom & Water Chlorination
authority: NDMA & Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)
summary: Emergency medical triage, life-support continuity, and post-inundation infectious disease prevention protocols.
official_directives: Maintain a ward-wise registry of dialysis patients, oxygen-dependent patients, and full-term pregnant women (EDD within 15 days) for pre-emptive ambulance transfer 24 hours before peak hazard.
Stock Polyvalent Anti-Snake Venom (ASV), Doxycycline (leptospirosis prophylaxis), ORS packets, and Halogen chlorine tablets at all Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and relief camps.
Mandate super-chlorination of municipal and camp drinking water to maintain 0.5–1.0 ppm free residual chlorine; prohibit consumption of unboiled flood-exposed well water.
Provide 14-day waterproof chronic medication kits (insulin in insulated cold packs, anti-hypertensives, cardiac drugs) to evacuated senior citizens.

manual_title: NDMA & DAHD Guidelines: Disaster Management for Livestock, Cattle & Companion Animals
section_ref: Section 9.1 — Untethering Mandate, Elevated Flood Mounds (Kanti) & Fodder Banks
authority: NDMA & Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD)
summary: Mandatory life-safety rules for preventing mass livestock mortality during riverine floods and coastal cyclone surges.
official_directives: CRITICAL RULE: Immediately UNCHAIN and untether all cattle, buffaloes, and goats prior to floodwater ingress or evacuation. Tethered animals drown rapidly, whereas free livestock can swim to high ground.
Herd livestock to elevated community earthen flood mounds (Kanti) or high highway embankments 12 hours ahead of river crest or cyclone landfall.
Store dry fodder, hay bales, and mineral mixtures on elevated bamboo platforms covered with waterproof tarpaulins to prevent fungal aflatoxin and rumen acidosis.
Conduct post-flood ring vaccination against Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) and Black Quarter (BQ) across all affected veterinary blocks.
